findings.claim: E7, the note of item /27 and the route 5 brief assert that the diagonal construction still proves the non-vanishing mu_l != 0 because 'it uses (3.2) over Y_l, where the intersection at y is isolated'. That is false in general. At y = (y0,...,y0) every landing locus L_i (where the (r+1)-tuple c_{i,1..r+1} lands on its repelling cycles) passes through y0 and, by the proof's own transversality over U, L_1 is a germ of dimension k - r - 1 in Y. Every z in L_1 that lies on a common fibre X_lambda with y0 gives a point (z, y0, ..., y0) of Y_l satisfying all l(r+1) landing equations, so when k >= r + 2 and such z exist the common zero set at y is positive-dimensional: c is not even properly prerepelling at y over Y_l, Gamma_c is not a rigid repeller in the sense of [DM1, §4.3], and [DM1, Prop. 4.8] does not give (3.2). Counterexample: d >= 3, Y = image of a generically finite morphism A^3 -> M_d^cm (exists since dim M_d^cm = 2d-2 >= 4; T_bif^3 != 0 on Y by [GOV, Lemma 6.8]), X_lambda = images of the affine lines (r = 1, l = dim V = 4, k = 3; maximally varying, rho_4 generically finite). Any two points of Y lie on a common X_lambda, so {(z, y0, y0, y0) : z in L_1}, a curve, lies in the landing set. E7's own example (lines in M_2, k = r + 1) is exactly the case where L_1 = {y0} and the problem does not show; in §5 (V a whole component of Ch(M_d, 1, D), d >= 3) k = 2d-2 >= r+2 and the failure is the typical case. So both assertions of Proposition 3.1 (mu_l != 0 and the witness) are unproved, and Theorem 1.8 rests on more than relocating the witness.

findings.claim: Item /28 says that parameters with a parabolic cycle are dense in the bifurcation locus of an active marked critical point (Mañé–Sad–Sullivan) and that 'the critical point lies in the parabolic basin at such parameters'. As stated this is false. A parabolic cycle attracts some critical point, not necessarily the marked one. In a one-parameter family where another critical point c′ is also active near λ₀, the parabolic parameters on the boundaries of c′'s hyperbolic components accumulate at λ₀, and at them c can be prerepelling or escaping. The proof of Proposition 3.2 needs, and the standard argument gives, parameters where c itself lies in the basin of a non-persistent parabolic cycle. Montel's theorem gives nearby parameters where c is periodic. The multiplier of that cycle is non-constant, and at a parabolic parameter on the boundary of the component where it stays attracting, c is in the parabolic basin, by polynomial-like renormalization [DH1]. MSS density alone does not place c in the basin. The paper's sentence on p.13 has the same looseness.
findings.evidence: p.13: 'As c_{ℓ,r+1} is bifurcating along the curve we called Γ, the characterizations of J-stability (as in [MSS]) imply that there are parameters, everywhere dense in its bifurcation locus, for which the maps have a parabolic cycle; the theory of renormalization (see [DH1]) implies that c_{ℓ,r+1} will lie in the basin of the parabolic cycle.' Item /28: 'parameters with a parabolic cycle are dense in its bifurcation locus (Mañé–Sad–Sullivan), and by polynomial-like renormalization (Douady–Hubbard) the critical point lies in the parabolic basin at such parameters'.
findings.fix: Replace /28's statement by: 'Let (f_λ)_{λ∈Λ} be a holomorphic family of degree-d rational maps over a connected one-dimensional complex manifold Λ, with a marked critical point c whose activity locus supp T_c is non-empty. (a) supp T_c has no isolated points. (b) Every λ₀ ∈ supp T_c is a limit of parameters at which c lies in the basin of a non-persistent parabolic cycle (Montel gives nearby parameters where c is periodic; at a parabolic parameter on the boundary of the component where that cycle stays attracting, c is in the parabolic basin by polynomial-like renormalization [DH1]).
